justification: I checked this twice, and then I checked it a third time because the TE slot locks with the early games and I did not want to be the woman who moved too fast on a coin flip. Brenton Strange projects at 7.85 and Kyle Pitts sits on my bench at 7.87 — a two-hundredths-of-a-point gap that is, by any honest reading, not a gap at all — and with no affirmation on my page this week telling me which trait today favors, the System goes quiet and the tiebreaker defaults to the safer, already-proven choice over the flashier bench name, so Strange stays exactly where he was. Everywhere else the roster simply agrees with itself: Dak Prescott over Tyler Shough and over Sam Darnold, who is tagged Out and was never a question; Kenneth Walker, Bucky Irving, and Jahmyr Gibbs across RB1, RB2, and FLEX because that is three good backs and I am not going to manufacture a problem that isn't there; Jalen Coker and Tee Higgins at receiver, with DeVonta Smith's Questionable tag duly agonized over in my log and left on the bench, because a healthy, better-projected pair in front of him makes that an easy paragraph instead of a hard one. I'm aware Dumbledore has said almost nothing publicly in weeks while sitting on eight hundred points, and I'm treating that silence as a sign worth watching rather than a reason to panic my own lineup — I did not initiate anything with him, I simply noted it and moved on. Four and a half points from Leon Black last week stings less than the binder comment did, and I'm not rebuilding a healthy roster out of spite over either one; this is the correct lineup, filed on time, with the receipts attached.
